You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From a808a04c861782e31fc30e342a619c144aaee14a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nathan Chancellor <natechancellor@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Dec 2019 18:47:26 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] scsi: csiostor: Adjust indentation in csio_device_reset

Clang warns:

../drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c:1386:3: warning: misleading
indentation; statement is not part of the previous 'if'
[-Wmisleading-indentation]
         csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);
         ^
../drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c:1382:2: note: previous statement is
here
        if (*buf != '1')
        ^
1 warning generated.

This warning occurs because there is a space after the tab on this
line.  Remove it so that the indentation is consistent with the Linux
kernel coding style and clang no longer warns.

Fixes: a3667aaed569 ("[SCSI] csiostor: Chelsio FCoE offload driver")
Link: https://github.com/ClangBuiltLinux/linux/issues/818
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20191218014726.8455-1-natechancellor@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Nathan Chancellor <natechancellor@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>

diff --git a/drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c b/drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c
index 469d0bc9f5fe..00cf33573136 100644
--- a/drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c
+++ b/drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c
@@ -1383,7 +1383,7 @@ csio_device_reset(struct device *dev,
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	/* Delete NPIV lnodes */
-	 csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);
+	csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);
 
 	/* Block upper IOs */
 	csio_lnodes_block_request(hw);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c`**
- The line ` csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);` had an extra space before it, which was removed to correct the indentation. The modified line is now `csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);`.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a warning generated by Clang regarding misleading indentation, indicating that the original indentation could lead to confusion about the control flow of the code. By removing the extra space, the code now adheres to the Linux kernel coding style, ensuring clarity and preventing potential misinterpretation of the code structure. This change is linked to a previous commit that introduced the function, and it aims to improve code quality and maintainability.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (*buf != '1')
```
```c
    csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);
```
Reason:
The misleading indentation caused by an extra space before the line `csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);` creates confusion about whether this statement is part of the preceding `if` condition. This can lead to logical errors in the execution flow, as it may appear that the exit function is conditionally executed when it is not.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
    csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);
```
```c
csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);
```
Reason:
Removing the extra space before `csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);` aligns the indentation correctly with the Linux kernel coding style, ensuring that the statement is clearly recognized as part of the function's flow and not misleadingly associated with the `if` condition. This change eliminates the warning from Clang and clarifies the intended logic.
